guest-init.sh.content_utf8:
#!/bin/sh
export PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/sbin:/usr/sbin
export HOME=/root CI=true EARTHLY_DISABLE_ANALYTICS=true EARTHLY_CI=true
umask 077
if [ "${1:-}" != "mounted-root" ]; then
    mkdir -p /run/regular-root
    mount -t tmpfs -o size=1630m tmpfs /run/regular-root || poweroff -f
    for data in /bin /usr /lib /sbin /etc /case /opt /root /init; do
        cp -a "$data" /run/regular-root/ || poweroff -f
    done
    mkdir -p /run/regular-root/proc /run/regular-root/sys /run/regular-root/dev /run/regular-root/run /run/regular-root/tmp
    chmod 1777 /run/regular-root/tmp
    exec switch_root /run/regular-root /init mounted-root
fi
mount -t proc proc /proc
mount -t sysfs sys /sys
mount -t cgroup2 none /sys/fs/cgroup
mount -t devtmpfs dev /dev
mkdir -p /dev/pts /dev/shm /run/buildkit
mount -t devpts devpts /dev/pts
mount -t tmpfs shm /dev/shm
ip link set lo up
ip addr add 192.0.2.17/32 dev lo
trap 'printf "CORPUS-EARTHLY-FAIL\n"; tail -65 /tmp/buildkit.log; poweroff -f' EXIT
set -eu
fixture-registry >/tmp/registry.log 2>&1 &
endpoint=tcp://192.0.2.17:8372
buildkitd --config /etc/buildkit/buildkitd.toml --root /run/buildkit-data --addr "$endpoint" --oci-worker-snapshotter=native --oci-worker-net=host --containerd-worker=false >/tmp/buildkit.log 2>&1 &
bk=$!
i=0
while ! buildctl --addr "$endpoint" debug workers >/dev/null 2>&1; do
    kill -0 "$bk"
    sleep 1
    i=$((i+1))
    [ "$i" -lt 25 ]
done
cd /case
echo "CORPUS-EARTHLY-START"
sha256sum Earthfile
earthly --version
earthly --config /etc/earthly-local.yml --buildkit-host "$endpoint" +greeting
if [ ! -f greeting.txt ]; then
    earthly --config /etc/earthly-local.yml --buildkit-host "$endpoint" --artifact +greeting/greeting.txt ./greeting.txt
fi
[ "$(wc -c < greeting.txt | tr -d ' ')" = "14" ]
echo "CORPUS-ARTIFACT"
cat greeting.txt
sha256sum greeting.txt
echo "CORPUS-EARTHLY-COMPLETE"
trap - EXIT
poweroff -f

toolchain: Earthly 0.8.16 and matching earthly/buildkitd v0.8.16 in offline Alpine Linux guest
semantic_scope: The native Earthly build ran the unchanged Earthfile. The guest verified and exported the exact 14-byte greeting.txt artifact using the recorded Alpine base image.
